content.value_statement: Pricing decisions lose consistency when teams skip regular reviews. This skill organizes quarterly metrics, meeting agendas, decision records, and follow-up ownership.
actual_capabilities: Define quarterly focus areas and a recurring ten-metric data checklist.
Generate a six-section, 90-minute agenda using supplied pricing metrics.
Highlight metric anomalies against the trailing four-quarter mean using a one-standard-deviation threshold.
Organize decisions as HOLD, ITERATE, or ESCALATE TO TRIBUNAL.
Capture metrics, decisions, actions, attendees, and the next review date in a structured review log.
Plan quarterly reviews, 30-day action check-ins, and escalation meetings.
limitations: CRM and billing data must be supplied; the skill includes no authenticated data connectors.
Companion pricing skills and framework references are not included in the reviewed package.
Calendar scheduling requires external access; this file provides instructions, not a calendar integration.
Reliable anomaly checks require historical data, and pricing thresholds still need business-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Prepare the revenue review
use_cases.description: Assemble CRM and billing metrics, identify data gaps, and prepare the quarterly pricing agenda.

use_cases.title: Review discount discipline
use_cases.description: Evaluate discount trends and policy compliance, then propose specific actions with accountable owners.

use_cases.title: Govern pricing decisions
use_cases.description: Distinguish routine adjustments from material pricing changes and document the appropriate decision and follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a first review
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare our first Q2 pricing review checklist and 90-minute agenda. List required attendees and flag data we must provide.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish the quarterly review process.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze quarterly metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the attached quarterly metrics and four-quarter history to populate the agenda. Flag anomalies and missing data without inventing values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare an evidence-based meeting agenda.

prompt_templates.title: Document review decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these meeting notes to classify decisions as HOLD, ITERATE, or ESCALATE. Draft actions, owners, check-in dates, and a review-log entry.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: convert meeting notes into accountable follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a pricing escalation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the attached segmented metrics, discount policy, and buyer feedback. Compare routine adjustments with material changes, then propose a verdict and escalation rationale.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate mixed pricing signals before making a material change.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Q2 review using a 19% mean discount, up from 12%, with policy compliance at 72%.
output: Quarter focus: Discount discipline and pocket-price waterfall refresh.
Agenda: Data check-in; discount review; tier distribution; willingness-to-pay signals; decisions; calendar and ownership.
Discussion priority: Examine the discount increase and investigate policy exceptions.
Data gap: Four-quarter history is required before calculating the anomaly threshold.

output_examples.input: The team chose ITERATE and assigned discount-policy changes to the sales leader, with a 30-day check-in.
output: Action: Draft the agreed discount-policy changes.
Follow-up: Check progress in 30 days and plan the next quarterly review in 90 days.
Review-log gaps: Confirm the meeting date, attendees, metrics snapshot, and exact policy changes.

best_practices: Provide consistent metric definitions and four quarters of history, with relevant customer segments.
Include pricing, sales, finance or revenue operations, and product leaders in every review.
Record decisions, reasoning, action owners, and follow-up dates after the meeting.
anti_patterns: Inventing missing metric values or treating illustrative pricing thresholds as universal targets.
Using competitor prices as the primary basis for pricing decisions.
Making material pricing changes without escalation or documenting only vague action items.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It prepares a pricing data checklist, a 90-minute agenda, decision categories, a review record, and follow-up plans.

faq.question: Does it retrieve CRM or billing data automatically?
faq.answer: No. It identifies required data sources, but you must supply exports or arrange authorized access through separate integrations.

faq.question: What historical data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide current metrics and the preceding four quarters where available. Missing history limits trend analysis and anomaly detection.

faq.question: What are the decision categories?
faq.answer: HOLD means no current change. ITERATE covers specific routine adjustments. ESCALATE TO TRIBUNAL routes material or strategic changes for further evaluation.

faq.question: Does it schedule calendar events automatically?
faq.answer: The instructions request scheduling, but the reviewed file includes no calendar integration. Actual booking requires separate authorized access.

faq.question: Can this skill operate without its companion skills?
faq.answer: The checklist and agenda are self-contained. Waterfall refreshes, escalation design, and renewal guidance reference companion documents outside the reviewed package.
